title: Singapore Regulators crackdown on PGL Major over gambling concerns
content:
BC.Game will not be allowed to use its own name or logo at the PGL Major Singapore, after the crypto casino’s chief executive confirmed that Singapore’s gambling rules apply to its Counter-Strike 2 team. “Yes we are not allowed to use our logo and name due to regulations in Singapore, it’s not Valve,” Ali “Ako” Muhanned wrote on X on 6 November. He added that he had known about the restriction for a long time, and that the team had already submitted an alternative that was still waiting for approval. His post came a day after the Russian Telegram channel Esports Base reported that BC.Game, BetBoom Team, 1win and PARIVISION would all have to play the PGL Major Singapore under different names.

According to that report, logos, stickers and team names that include or point to a gambling, casino or bookmaker brand are barred at the event unless the brand holds a valid Singapore licence. The four organisations were reportedly given about a day to propose neutral alternatives. Neither PGL nor Valve has published a statement on the requirements, and BetBoom, 1win and PARIVISION have not said which names they will use. BetBoom Team’s general director, Artyom “Pioneer” Savelyev, did write in his Telegram channel that “BoomBoys will not play at the Major in Singapore”. That rules out the name the club used at Dota 2’s biggest event this year.

The rules behind the change come from Singapore’s Gambling Control Act 2022, which is enforced by the Gambling Regulatory Authority (GRA). Section 85 of the act makes it an offence to advertise any unlawful gambling, which covers gambling services that are not licensed or exempted in Singapore. Crucially for esports teams, the section treats sponsorship and brand-sharing deals as advertising when a name is displayed in connection with an event and gambling is the main activity carried out under that name. On that reading, a team named after a casino or bookmaker brand would appear to fall squarely within the definition, whatever the players themselves do on the server.

The penalties are serious enough to make any event organiser cautious. A conviction under section 85 carries a fine of up to S$20,000, and the offence is one of strict liability, so prosecutors do not need to prove that anyone meant to advertise gambling. Under section 87 , the GRA can also order advertisers to remove the material and publish a corrective advertisement. Ignoring such an order can lead to a fine of up to S$50,000, two years in prison, or both. The authority already works to block unlicensed online gambling sites and payments, and it asks the public to report unlawful gambling advertisements and promotions.

Singapore has made room for gambling sponsors before, but only through a formal legal exemption. In October 2025, the Ministry of Home Affairs issued an exemption order for the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix , which runs until the end of 2028. It lets sponsors that provide unauthorised gambling services show their names and logos on racing team attire, cars and even team names, provided there is no invitation to gamble. That order names only the Grand Prix, which means it offers nothing to the 32 teams arriving for the Major.

For three of the four teams, playing under another name at a Valve event is nothing new. At The International 2026 in Shanghai in August, BetBoom Team played as BoomBoys, PARIVISION as Team Vision and 1win as Iron Wing. Valve never explained the changes publicly, although Savelyev later said the club had to rename because of restrictions on bookmaker branding at the event. Team Vision went all the way to the grand final, where they lost 3-2 to Team Spirit, so the new name did little to slow them down.

title: GTA 6 Mural in Brooklyn Ruined with Graffiti two weeks before launch
content:
A hand-painted Grand Theft Auto VI mural in Brooklyn, New York, has been tagged with graffiti less than a month after it was finished, and just over two weeks before the game comes out. The wall at the corner of Wythe Avenue and North 11th Street in Williamsburg shows Jason and Lucia, the game’s two leads, in the same artwork that Rockstar Games uses for its launch trailer.

Late on Tuesday night, according to reports, someone sprayed a large black-and-white “JELOUS” tag across the bottom of the piece. Photos of the tagged wall were then shared on Instagram by an account called jelous.ktd, and many GTA fans have not taken it well.

The tag runs across the lower half of the mural, over the legs of both characters and the front of the red car that Lucia is sitting on. The Grand Theft Auto logo, the faces of both characters and the Rockstar logo in the corner are all still visible. As of Friday, neither Rockstar nor Colossal Media, the New York company that painted the wall, had commented publicly on the damage. There has also been no report that the mural has been cleaned or repainted since the tag appeared.

The mural is the work of Colossal Media , a company that specialises in hand-painted outdoor advertising and is based nearby on North 10th Street. Colossal confirmed the job in an Instagram post on 3 October , saying it had painted its first ever campaign for Rockstar 22 years ago. “Two decades later, we’re back at it for GTA 6,” the company wrote, describing the jump from San Andreas in 2004 to GTA VI in 2026 as a tradition that continues. That post has since collected more than 200,000 likes on Instagram.

The corner itself has some Rockstar history, having carried a Grand Theft Auto V mural back in 2013, according to the fan site GTABoom. Colossal’s painters spent about seven days on the new piece, which was finished around 10 October after fans had tracked its progress through photos posted on Reddit. One freelance muralist, who said in Reddit comments that he was working on the wall for Colossal, described it as a temporary piece with a lifespan of around a month. TalkEsport has not been able to verify that account, and neither Rockstar nor Colossal has said how long the mural will stay up.

The reaction online was quick, and most of it was hostile. Under the Instagram post showing the tag, commenters wrote “Ruined” and “Not cool”, according to Kotaku, even as the photo became one of the account’s most popular posts. TheGamer later reported that comments on the post had been switched off after the criticism kept coming. On the GTA subreddit, a user who said they were an Italian graffiti artist called it “pretty disrespectful, even by graffiti standards”.

title: FUT Esports Sign Wo0t From Team Heretics, With batujnax and hezacoil Reportedly Next for VCT 2027
content:
FUT Esports have started rebuilding their Valorant team for VCT 2027, and the first name is a big one. The Turkish organisation announced on 6 November that Mert “ Wo0t ” Alkan is “officially joining our VCT roster”, adding that the move is still pending Riot approval. Within minutes of that announcement, Sheep Esports reported that Fire Flux Esports initiator Mehmet Batu “batujnax” Özaslan has reached a verbal agreement to join him. That followed an earlier report from the same outlet that his Fire Flux teammate Berkay “hezacoil” Doğar is heading the same way.

A NEW ERA BEGINS. @WootVL is officially joining our VCT roster! Welcome to the family, let’s make history together! pic.twitter.com/WNaFn3DKI7

Wo0t is the headline signing, and he arrives with one of the best records of any Turkish player in the VCT. He spent three years with Team Heretics , reaching the Valorant Champions 2024 grand final and winning the Esports World Cup in 2025. He then lifted the VCT EMEA Stage 1 title with the Spanish club this year, before leaving it on 22 October. He has also worn the FUT shirt before, standing in for the team at Monsters Reloaded 2026 last month, where FUT finished in the top four.

The changes follow a season that ended in disappointment at Valorant Champions in Shanghai. FUT opened the group stage with a 2-0 win over JD Gaming, but losses to 100 Thieves and T1 sent them home early, in an event that LOUD went on to win . Back in Europe, FUT had finished third at VCT EMEA Stage 2 after a 3-0 defeat to Team Liquid in the lower bracket final. That was enough to qualify for Champions, but not enough to change the feeling that the roster had peaked.

FUT have already parted ways with Doğan “xeus” Gözgen, Efe “s0pp” Tur and Volkan “sociablEE” Yönal, along with head coach Berke “Vlad” Kantürk, according to Sheep Esports, whose reporting cites Riot’s VCT Global Contract Database. Eray “yetujey” Budak is signed only until the end of 2026, while Okan “KROSTALY” Alaçam has a deal that runs through the 2027 season, although it is not clear whether he will stay. The organisation kept its partner slot when Riot cut each international league to eight teams for the 2027-28 cycle, so it has the security to rebuild properly.

Neither batujnax nor hezacoil is a household name yet, but both have climbed quickly through the Turkish scene. batujnax made his VCT debut with Apeks in 2025, after the team earned promotion through Ascension EMEA. Both players then spent the early part of 2026 at S2G Esports. From there, he and hezacoil moved to REBORN, winning Challengers EMEA Stage 2 and finishing second in Stage 3, before Fire Flux Esports took over the roster in August.

title: WoW: Forever Dodged the Launch Queues, Now Blizzard Has to Fix Its Ghost Towns
content:
World of Warcraft: Forever has had the kind of launch that MMO players rarely get, with servers up on time and queues measured in minutes rather than hours. Blizzard’s new take on the 2004 game went live in every region at once at 3pm PST on 4 November, which was midnight in Paris, and it has drawn wide coverage in France this week. As one French headline put it, Blizzard is betting big on a return to its roots. The problem, two days in, is that parts of that old world feel strangely empty, and Blizzard has promised to adjust things on Friday.

Forever is not a straight re-release like WoW Classic, which recreates the original game as it was. Instead, it imagines what would have happened if Blizzard had kept building on the Azeroth of 2004. It keeps the level cap at 60 and adds new zones, quests, dungeons and raids to the original world. It runs alongside both modern World of Warcraft and Classic, and access is included with a standard WoW subscription , which costs €13 a month in France, according to AFP.

The complaints started within hours of launch, once the crowds in the starting zones had spread out across the world. Players on the official forums reported capital cities with only a handful of other people in them, even though PC Gamer reported hundreds of thousands of players online. It pinned the problem on the game’s “realmless layering technology”, which splits a huge population into many copies of the same world. That can leave a city like Stormwind looking deserted, which is a real problem for a game built on nostalgia for crowded auction houses and busy roads.

Blizzard has acknowledged the issue and moved quickly to address it. In a forum reply on 5 November , Blizzard’s Aggrend wrote that the team was aware of “some issues with certain areas not feeling as populated as they should”. He added that Blizzard would be “tweaking some numbers tomorrow to help things feel a bit more lively”, which points to changes on Friday. He did not say which numbers would change, or by how much.

The smooth start owes a lot to a difficult beta. Blizzard raised server capacity twice during the public test because of demand and queues, according to AFP, and the company said on X that nearly nine million characters were created during the testing period. Clayton Stone, Blizzard’s associate director of production, said in a Blizzard video that the beta had far exceeded the team’s expectations and was one of the biggest the company had ever run.

The new content is substantial for a game that refuses to raise its level cap. Forever adds three new zones and opens up areas such as Mount Hyjal, along with more than 1,000 quests, nine dungeons and two planned raids. A new race, the Skyborne Elves, also joins the game alongside new combinations such as Forsaken Paladins and Dwarf Shamans. Progression is deliberately horizontal, which means new gear and abilities should broaden a character’s options rather than make older content trivial. Access to the Skyborne Elves comes through optional upgrade packs, which also include cosmetics and game time, and a restock of the physical Collector’s Edition is not due to ship until February 2027.

title: FISSURE’s unpaid CS2, Dota 2 prize debt explained as CEO addresses financial struggles
content:
FISSURE burst onto the competitive schedule for Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) and Dota 2 in 2025. The organizer had started a new esports series for these games named FISSURE Playground.

Notably, the tournaments offered $1M+ prize pools and scheduled several events per season. After just one year, FISSURE Playground went into the shadows, canceling its 2026 tournaments.

The series resurfaced in September following a partnership contract with another organization — CS2 FISSURE Playground #3 took place in China.

For esports fans, competitive action is usually the main focus. However, FISSURE created significant financial turmoil behind the scenes, so the community had no choice but to notice unpaid debts owed to major teams like G2 Esports, Team Falcons, FURIA, and others.

In early November 2026, FISSURE’s CEO issued an official statement addressing the crisis and outlining their recovery plans.

Read on to discover the timeline behind FISSURE’s rapid rise and sudden collapse, along with the key factors that brought the organizer to this point.

title: Sony Cancels Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, Its Free-to-Play Mobile Shooter
content:
Sony has cancelled Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, its free-to-play mobile multiplayer shooter, a year after it entered soft launch. The game will leave mobile stores on November 21, 2026, and its servers will shut down on May 1, 2027, after which it will no longer be playable.

Ranger Rumble was developed by French mobile studio Oh BiBi in partnership with Insomniac Games, and published by PlayStation. It never got a full worldwide release. The team said on the game’s official website that it had “made the difficult decision to cease development,”.

Sony announced Ranger Rumble in November 2025 and launched it the same month in the Philippines and Indonesia, two markets often used to test mobile games before a wider release. It later expanded to Norway, Sweden, Finland, Denmark, France, Canada and the UK.

The game was pitched as a “fast-paced multiplayer platformer arena shooter”, taking Ratchet & Clank’s weapons and characters into short competitive matches built for phones. A year of testing across nine countries was apparently not enough to convince Sony to take it global. The official statement does not give a reason for the cancellation.

If you already have the game installed, you can keep playing until May. New players will not be able to download it after November 21.

The final update changes the game’s economy for its last six months. In-app purchases have been removed, and the Super Pass is now free for every player. Qwark Pass seasons will keep running until the shutdown, so players can still earn rewards just by playing.

title: PGL Will Fine CS2 Teams $30,000 for Withdrawing From Its Events
content:
PGL will fine CS2 teams $30,000 for pulling out of its events after their place is confirmed. The tournament organiser has added the penalty to its 2027 rulebook, along with a requirement to repay travel costs and cover the cost of a replacement team.

“This is done to create a more professional scene,” PGL CEO Silviu Stroie told HLTV . The move is aimed squarely at a habit that has grown under Valve’s ranking system, where teams sign up for events and then drop out when a better option for their ranking comes along.

The new rules apply to teams that withdraw from a PGL Main Event once their participation has been confirmed. According to the PGL 2027 rulebook , the organisation has to pay three things.

There is also a non-financial penalty that was already in the rulebook. Any roster that withdraws from a PGL event loses the chance of a direct VRS invite to the next PGL event that sends out invitations, whatever the reason for the withdrawal.

PGL has carved out two exceptions. Teams will not have to pay the fine or the costs if the withdrawal is caused by a documented medical emergency, or by a visa refusal that was outside the team’s control. That second point is narrow. A visa refused because a team applied late or sent an incomplete application does not count. In both cases, PGL wants official paperwork.

The invite ban still applies even in those cases, since that rule covers every withdrawal regardless of circumstances.

title: IEM Beijing Quarterfinals Recap: NAVI and BetBoom Advance to Semifinals
content:
IEM Beijing 2026 has reached its semi-finals following back-to-back exciting clashes, giving us the two teams that will be heading to the next stage. NAVI’s reverse sweep ensured they made it to the semis while BETBOOM stunned FURIA, surviving a tough series that could have gone either way.

3-0 to start Mirage, NAVI had a solid start until they lost the momentum to PARIVISION. Winning their first gun round, PARIVISION went on to secure a dominant half. Not only did they level the scoreline, but they won every single round until the half ended, giving them a 9-3 lead before switching sides. Surviving the beating, NAVI managed to find their momentum despite losing the pistol in the second half. Winning 9 of their own, NAVI forced the map to OT from the clutches of defeat. Coming into OT with momentum, NAVI’s rushed offence gave PARIVISION the room they needed to secure 3 rounds in a row and close the map 16-13.

Starting Inferno with 4 rounds in a row, PARIVISION continued their momentum from the first map before NAVI hit the scoreboard. Following a difficult start, NAVI managed to cut it closer, winning 3 rounds in a row to close the first half. Salvaging the first half, NAVI managed to dominate on their T-side as PARIVISION failed to secure anything more than 2 rounds. With a 13-9 win, NAVI levelled the series, taking us to the deciding map.

With a convincing win in Inferno, NAVI started Ancient on a solid note, leaving PARIVISION to play chase for the better part of the final map. As the first half progressed, PARIVISION closed in on NAVI as the half switched with a 7-5 lead. The second half saw both teams trade rounds, with NAVI narrowly edging it out in the end with the series closing 2-1. Delivering an AWP masterclass, w0nderful secured a 1.54 IR.

. @natusvincere complete the reverse sweep @parivisiongg to secure their spot in the semi-finals of #IEM Beijing 2026 Mirage 14-16 Inferno 13-9 Ancient 13-10 pic.twitter.com/DDcRgm0AgQ

Starting the map with a pistol round win, BETBOOM conceded the first round against the FURIA full buy. As the Brazilian side struggled to hold onto the momentum, BetBoom managed to secure the lead before the end of the first half with a 7-5 scoreline. Following a tightly contested first half, BETBOOM raced ahead with a well-drilled defence that saw them win 6 rounds in a row, closing the map with a dominant 13-5 victory.

title: LEC : Ibai (KOI) prêt à « péter » le salary cap pour un « équipazo » !
content:
Movistar KOI prépare son mercato pour la saison 2027 du LEC. Ibai Llanos, streamer et cofondateur du club, s’est exprimé en direct sur le sujet, et il promet « un véritable équipazo » pour l’an prochain, quel qu’en soit le coût. Il envisage même de dépasser le salary cap pour y parvenir à en croire les informations de Marca .

Le dirigeant assume ainsi de sortir le chéquier. Ce ne sont pour l’instant que des intentions : aucun renfort n’est officialisé à ce jour.

Le chantier s’articule autour d’une ossature déjà verrouillée. Melzhet, entraîneur, ainsi que les joueurs Elyoya, Jojopyun et Álvaro semblent tous assurés de rester, leurs prolongations ayant été signées dans l’année. Autour de ce noyau, deux dossiers restent ouverts.

Le cas de Supa est le plus sensible. Joueur en fin de contrat, il n’a pas renouvelé et a été très critiqué après l’élimination des Worlds 2026. Myrwn, lui aussi en fin de contrat, n’a pas non plus renouvelé. Deux places sont donc à pourvoir dans un roster appelé à changer.

En toplane, les noms de BrokenBlade (G2) et Naak Nako (Vitality) circulent avec insistance. Selon les informations du quotidien espagnol, ce dossier serait le plus avancé en interne. Pour le poste d’ADC, les pistes évoquées sont en revanche moins solides : Berserker, Jopa, Ice, Flakked ou Upset figurent parmi les noms qui circulent. Autant de pistes, aucune signature.

La phrase qui résume l’ambition du dirigeant est tombée en espagnol : « Si hace falta me ‘peto’ el límite salarial » , a lancé Ibai, ce que l’on peut traduire par « s’il le faut, je fais sauter le plafond salarial » . Une formule d’intention, pas une décision actée : aucun dépassement n’est à ce jour confirmé.

title: Zicssi va découvrir le LEC avec SK Gaming
content:
C’était l’un des joueurs les plus attendus sur le marché des transferts, et son avenir semble désormais se dessiner. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Lanzo « Zicssi » Ciajolo aurait trouvé un accord verbal avec SK Gaming pour la saison 2027 du LEC. Le Français était également en discussions avec Vitality, GIANTX et Fnatic, mais aucune de ces trois organisations n’était prête à lui transmettre une offre concrète, privilégiant d’autres pistes. Plutôt que de prendre le risque de voir les portes du LEC se refermer, le jungler de Solary aurait donc choisi d’accepter la proposition de SK Gaming, où il devrait remplacer son compatriote Skeanz, annoncé du côté de Galions en LFL.

Cette promotion vient récompenser une année 2026 particulièrement réussie. Véritable moteur de Solary, Zicssi a largement contribué au retour au premier plan de la structure française, avec trois titres majeurs : le LFL Invitational, les EMEA Masters Winter et le Spring Split de la LFL. Sur le plan individuel, il a également été élu MVP de ces trois compétitions, dont la finale des EMEA Masters Winter. Son style agressif, notamment sur des champions comme Xin Zhao, Wukong ou Vi, a fait des ravages tout au long de la saison. Solary est même passé tout près d’un sacre international historique au World Star Challengers Invitational, s’inclinant 3-2 en finale face à l’équipe académique de T1.

Chez SK Gaming, Zicssi devrait retrouver un autre Français, Thomas « 3XA » Foucou, lui aussi attendu dans l’effectif pour 2027. Le duo rejoindrait Seo « SlowQ » Ye-bit, seul rescapé de la saison précédente, ainsi que le support coréen Park « Lospa » Joon-hyeong, annoncé en provenance de Fnatic. Une reconstruction presque totale pour l’organisation allemande, qui sort d’une nouvelle année très compliquée en LEC. Incapable de se qualifier pour les playoffs lors des trois splits de 2026, SK avait même subi une élimination embarrassante face à Galions lors des qualifications européennes pour l’Esports World Cup.

L’arrivée de Zicssi pourrait donc apporter un nouveau souffle à une équipe en quête de résultats. Le Français deviendrait également le deuxième joueur de Solary à rejoindre le LEC après le support Piero, attendu chez GIANTX. Un joli symbole pour une formation qui a longtemps dominé la scène française cette année, malgré ses deux défaites face à Galions en finale des EMEA Masters. Pour Zicssi, le défi sera désormais de confirmer au plus haut niveau européen, dans un championnat où plusieurs junglers de renom devraient également changer d’équipe, à l’image de Lyncas vers G2 et Razork vers Team Heretics.

title: Pokémon Fans Camp Outside a French Fnac a Day Early for the 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection
content:
Around ten Pokémon fans set up folding chairs outside the Fnac in Chartres from early on Thursday afternoon, wrapped in scarves against the November cold. According to the local paper L’Écho Républicain, they were ready to spend the night on the pavement. They were waiting for the Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection, the flagship box of Pokémon’s 30th anniversary range, which went on sale on Friday 6 November. “J’ai décidé d’arriver beaucoup plus tôt”, one fan told the paper, which translates as “I decided to arrive much earlier”. L’Écho Républicain described the scene as rare enough to be worth telling, although it has become a familiar one across France since the anniversary cards first arrived in September.

The reason for the early start becomes clear once you look inside the box. According to The Pokémon Company , each Ultra-Premium Collection contains 29 booster packs from the 30th Celebration expansion, plus a special pack with three cards from the set’s nostalgic Classic Collection. It also includes a foil Pikachu ex promo illustrated by the Japanese artist YOSHIROTTEN, alongside a playmat, 65 sleeves, a deck box, a metal coin, six damage-counter dice and a Pokémon TCG Live code card. The box comes in two versions: a day-themed edition built around Espeon ex, known in France as Mentali, and a night-themed edition built around Umbreon ex, or Noctali, each with its own foil promo.

For French collectors, the launch has not been quite as simple as it was in the United States. The Pokémon Company’s American product page lists 6 November for both editions, but the French product page still gives only a fourth-quarter window for the Journée and Soirée boxes. Most French retailers have listed the Soirée box with Noctali for 6 November and the Journée box with Mentali for 27 November, a split that has circulated since late October without an official explanation.

The price gap between the two markets is just as noticeable. Most French shops list the Ultra-Premium Collection at €229.99, and a few at €239.99. In the US, the trade publication ICv2 reported a suggested retail price of $179.99, and American prices are usually quoted before sales tax. The same Friday also brought two smaller anniversary products, the Ditto Premium Collection and a Figure Collection with either Mew or Mewtwo, both of which The Pokémon Company dated to 6 November. French retailers list the Ditto box, called Métamorph in France, at €49.99, while the Mew and Mewtwo sets cost €37.99 each. All three follow the Espeon ex and Umbreon ex Battle Decks , which the US product page dated to 30 October.

Chartres is only the latest stop in a frenzy that began when the 30th Celebration expansion went on sale worldwide on 16 September. The anniversary itself fell on 27 February, exactly 30 years after Pocket Monsters Red and Green launched in Japan, and The Pokémon Company has spread its celebration products across the rest of the year. As we reported when the set was first revealed in June , it was the first Pokémon TCG expansion to receive a coordinated global launch. Every card in it is printed in foil, and every pack is guaranteed to contain a Pikachu. That combination of nostalgia and novelty has proved hard to resist for players, collectors and resellers alike.

In Paris, two cousins waited 23 hours outside the Fuji Store, whose stock sold out in under ten minutes after opening, according to the radio station Urban Hit. The shop’s manager, Karim, told the station that demand far exceeded supply, and the station found some customers ready to spend up to €1,000 on cards. La Nouvelle République reported that one customer even camped in a shop car park near Blois, while its report from Châteauroux carried a warning that there would not be enough for everyone.

title: Mirage and Dust 2 Pick Rates Drop With New CS2 Map Pick System
content:
On September 22, 2026, Valve rolled out a major CS2 update that completely changed some aspects of the game, adding silent reloads for all weapons, implementing the Rush game mode, and reintroducing clan tags back to the shooter, among other changes. The biggest change for Premier players, though, was to the map veto process.

Prior to the update, the two teams took turns banning maps until only one remained in the pool. With the September 22 update, Valve replaced that with a pick-based system. To put it simply, Team 1 picks one map, Team 2 picks two, and Team 1 picks a final one. One of the picked maps is then randomly selected for that game.

The old format had a clear downside. Less popular maps were repeatedly eliminated during the ban phase, while the more popular maps were played every other game.

But how is Valve’s new map veto system faring against that? With a few months of data now available, we can see how much the new system has changed what people actually play.

According to data from Leetify , Mirage and Dust 2 have taken the biggest hit with the map veto change. Before the update, the two maps dominated Premier, with Mirage peaking at around 25% of matches and Dust 2 trailing just behind at roughly 24%. Since the change, Mirage has dropped to 20.3% and Dust 2 to 19.8% as of October 20.

title: Jonathan Switches to a Three-Finger Layout in BGMI to Improve His Shotgun Play
content:
Jonathan has changed the way he plays BGMI. After years on a two-finger setup, the Team Apex Gaming founder revealed on a live stream that he has moved to a three-finger control layout, and said the main reason is to sharpen his shotgun fights.

It is a bigger deal than it sounds. Jonathan built his reputation, and a YouTube channel that just passed 8 million subscribers , on the two-finger style. Changing it now means relearning movements he has done thousands of times without thinking.

Jonathan told viewers that the new layout is mainly about close-range play. Shotgun fights in BGMI are decided in fractions of a second, and they ask a lot of your hands at once. You need to move, aim, jump or crouch and fire, often while peeking a corner.

On two fingers, both thumbs are busy. The left thumb moves and the right thumb aims, so firing or jumping means briefly lifting one of them off its job. A third finger, usually the index finger on top of the screen, takes over one of those actions. That lets a player keep aiming while they shoot, which is exactly what close-range fights reward.

Jonathan was upfront that the switch will not pay off straight away. He said it will take time before he can use the new layout properly, because he has to build fresh muscle memory and get comfortable with where everything now sits on the screen.

Anyone who has changed control layouts knows the feeling. Buttons you used to hit without looking are suddenly in the wrong place, and your old habits keep pulling you back. For a while, a player can feel worse with the new setup than the old one, even if it has a higher ceiling in the long run.

title: Worlds 2026 : la Karmine Corp face à T1, le choc de tous les espoirs
content:
La Karmine Corp a rendez-vous avec l’histoire. Pour sa première participation aux championnats du monde de League of Legends, le club français s’apprête à disputer l’un des matchs les plus importants de son existence. Face à lui, un adversaire qui n’a presque plus besoin d’être présenté : T1, son mythique midlaner Faker et ses trois sacres mondiaux consécutifs. Sur le papier, les Sud-Coréens partent largement favoris, mais les protégés de Kameto ont déjà prouvé qu’ils pouvaient faire trembler les géants asiatiques. Après une défaite face à T1 au MSI, les Français avaient pris leur revanche à l’Esports World Cup, s’imposant 2-1 pour rejoindre la grande finale. Un précédent qui donne forcément des idées au Blue Wall.

Et pour réaliser un nouvel exploit, KC pourra notamment compter sur son prodige Caliste « Caliste » Henry-Hennebert. Impressionnant depuis le début de la compétition, le jeune ADC français a terminé le Swiss Stage avec 763 dégâts par minute, le meilleur total de cette phase du tournoi. Mais ce vendredi, le défi sera immense face à la botlane coréenne composée de Peyz et Keria, l’une des plus redoutables de la planète. Un duel explosif qui pourrait faire basculer la rencontre. Sur la toplane, Canna aura également un rôle majeur à jouer face à Doran, parfois en difficulté cette saison. Autant de confrontations individuelles qui pourraient permettre aux Européens de trouver des ouvertures.

Car malgré son immense palmarès, T1 n’a pas toujours affiché un visage impérial cette année. Les champions du monde en titre ont parfois montré des signes de fébrilité, notamment lors de leur rencontre face à Movistar KOI pendant le Swiss Stage. Faker, Oner et Doran ont connu des passages plus compliqués, tandis que Peyz n’a pas systématiquement retrouvé son niveau exceptionnel de la saison régulière. Mais les Worlds restent le royaume de T1. Peu importe le continent, la compétition semble transformer Faker et ses coéquipiers, capables de se transcender lorsque les enjeux deviennent immenses. Une expérience incomparable des grands rendez-vous qui fait des Coréens les grands favoris de cette confrontation.

Mais impossible de condamner KC avant même le début des hostilités. Portés par une communauté passionnée et une confiance grandissante, les Français ont les armes pour faire douter le géant coréen. Il faudra toutefois livrer une prestation presque parfaite, limiter les erreurs et surtout ne jamais laisser Faker et ses coéquipiers dicter le rythme de la série. Après l’élimination de G2 et de KOI, la Karmine Corp porte désormais à elle seule les espoirs de toute l’Europe. Une victoire lui ouvrirait les portes d’une demi-finale face à Bilibili Gaming, tombeur de Dplus KIA (3-0). Mais avant de rêver plus grand, il faudra faire tomber une légende. Et quoi de plus beau, pour le Blue Wall, que d’écrire son histoire en renversant T1 sur la scène où les Coréens règnent depuis trois ans ?

title: After Activision apologizes, moves to trim real Itaewon crush footage from Modern Warfare 4, Korea’s game regulator is unimpressed
content:
Activision will remove real footage of the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 in an update on 12 November. The decision follows protests from the families of the 159 people who died, who condemned the clip’s use in the game’s opening cinematic. The publisher apologised on 30 October, a week after launch, saying it had never meant to evoke or make light of any real tragedy. South Korea’s game regulator has made it clear, however, that taking the clip out will not settle the matter, and it is now looking at how the footage got past the country’s age-rating process.

The clip lasts about three seconds and appears in a montage of news reports about a fictional North Korean invasion of the South, which is how the campaign opens. Players identified it as real broadcast footage of people performing CPR on a victim in Itaewon on 29 October 2022. That night, a Halloween crowd crush in a narrow alley became one of the worst peacetime disasters in South Korea’s recent history. Modern Warfare 4 had launched worldwide on 23 October, only six days before the fourth anniversary, and its Korean War setting had already dragged the game into South Korean politics .

The 10·29 Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and a coalition of civic groups issued a joint statement on 28 October. They said they could not help but be appalled that scenes of citizens performing CPR had been “used unchanged to create a scene in a game”. They added that many people who helped with the rescue, or simply witnessed the disaster, are still living with trauma, and called the use of the tragedy as entertainment highly inappropriate. The families also pointed to hateful comments online that mocked the disaster by linking the crush to the game’s war setting.

The Korea Game Users Association, which speaks for players rather than the industry, backed the demand on the same day. It said real disaster footage “unrelated to the game’s progression” had revived the families’ pain, and asked Activision to explain why the clip was needed, apologise to those affected and replace it. Activision’s first response, given to Yonhap News Agency, was far more guarded. It said a few real news scenes had been used to convey the game’s fictional story, and that it had no intention of referencing or trivialising the Itaewon disaster. It did not, however, say whether the footage would be removed.

The tone changed completely when Activision spoke again two days later, in a statement sent to Korean media on 30 October. It described Modern Warfare 4 as “a work of fiction created to provide realistic immersion” and apologised to the bereaved families and victims. It also said the footage “will be completely removed” in the 12 November update. Infinity Ward’s Season 1 patch notes , published on 5 November, contain only one line for the campaign, on performance fixes. They make no mention of the cinematic, which leaves next week’s update as the date to watch.

The row has also reached the government, which is where the bigger questions for Activision now sit. Yun Ho-jung, the head of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety , told a press briefing on 29 October that including the footage amounted to “secondary harm” and that “appropriate sanctions should be imposed”. He added that any decision to punish the game or block access to it belonged to the relevant agencies. That phrase carries real weight in South Korea, where the Cabinet passed a revision to the Itaewon special act in February to give legal grounds for punishing the secondary victimisation of those affected by the crush.

title: Fortnite Sprite Extraction Site Locations and How to Use Them in Treasure Hunters
content:
There are eight Sprite Extraction Sites in Fortnite’s Treasure Hunters mini-season, spread around Lantern Landing, Plunder Port and the other main points of interest. Unlike Portable Extractors, these sites are fixed and can be used over and over, which makes them the most reliable way to bank your Sprites before you get eliminated.

Here is where to find every site, how to use them and what else they offer.

The sites sit between major POIs rather than inside them, which keeps them a little quieter than the hot drops. Two areas have two sites each, so it is worth learning those first.

Sprite Extraction Sites first appeared in Chapter 7 Season 3 and carried over into Treasure Hunters, so if you played last season, the setup will feel familiar.

Once a Sprite goes into the crate, you cannot take it back out, so only deposit the ones you want to keep. The good news is that extracted Sprites are safe for good. Even if you are eliminated straight afterwards, they stay extracted, and you can view them later in the Sprite Garden.

Each site also has Sprite Dust Services, which let you spend Sprite Dust on three things:

title: VCT EMEA : ara, Flickless et westside quittent GIANTX (off.)
content:
Le club espagnol tourne la page. GIANTX annonce se séparer de trois joueurs de son effectif VALORANT : Eduard-George « ara » Hanceriuc, Karel « Flickless » Maeckelbergh et Miłosz « westside » Duda. Les trois hommes étaient les seuls à avoir été présents du début à la fin de l’année 2026 dans l’effectif.

Leurs destinations divergent. Flickless va rejoindre UCAM Esports Club, où il retrouvera kamyk, Filu et waddle. Westside, lui, rejoint Joblife. Ara, en revanche, se retrouve sans équipe : il est actuellement agent libre.

Ara et Flickless avaient rejoint l’équipe en avril 2025, tandis que westside a passé deux saisons chez GIANTX. C’est cette même année 2025 qui a marqué les esprits : les trois joueurs avaient été au cœur de la bonne performance de l’équipe en EMEA Stage 2, avec à la clé une qualification pour les Champions de Paris.

Présents du début à la fin de l’année 2026, ils étaient les seuls à incarner la continuité de l’effectif. Leur départ laisse un vide que le club n’a pas encore comblé, puisqu’il n’a pas encore annoncé de nouveaux joueurs.

La saison dernière, l’équipe a enchaîné deux 9-10e places en ligue, avant une 13-16e place en Stage 2, assortie d’un bilan de 1-4 en phase de groupes. Ces contre-performances précèdent les départs annoncés des trois cadres du roster. La prochaine échéance est connue : GIANTX est invité au play-in des qualifications européennes de l’EMEA Kickoff, qui débutent le 25 novembre.

Today, we say goodbye to three members of our VALORANT roster. Thank you, @ara999_ @Flickless_ @euwestside , for your dedication, hard work and all the memories we've shared. We wish you all the best in your next chapter pic.twitter.com/aeEFycUTlO

title: Krafton Quietly Registers a Brazilian Holding Company, KRAFTON BRASIL HOLDINGS
content:
Krafton has set up a holding company in Brazil. KRAFTON BRASIL HOLDINGS LTDA was registered in São Paulo on October 26, 2026, with 12 million reais in capital, and Krafton, Inc. is its only investor, according to Brazilian tax records first reported by Inven Global .

The PUBG and BGMI publisher has not announced the company or said what it will do. On the same day the entity was registered, Krafton reportedly said that no official decision had been made on a Brazilian subsidiary. The paperwork tells a different story.

A CNPJ certificate is Brazil’s official business registration, issued by the Federal Revenue Service (Receita Federal). The certificate for KRAFTON BRASIL HOLDINGS LTDA lists the company as active from its founding date.

A holding company owns and manages shares in other businesses. In other words, this looks less like a game studio or publishing office and more like a vehicle for future investments, acquisitions or local subsidiaries.

The Brazilian company did not appear out of nowhere. According to Inven Global, Krafton has created a Brazil Strategy Development Department at its headquarters to plan its medium- and long-term strategy for Latin America. It is led by Kim Hyo-sub, who ran Bluehole, the studio behind PUBG and Krafton’s predecessor, from 2017 to 2020. Industry watchers also say Krafton chairman Chang Byung-gyu has long seen Latin America as the company’s next big hub.

Brazil is one of the largest gaming markets in the world by players, even if spending lags behind. Inven Global cites these figures:

title: Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone Season 1 Tune 17 Guns, With Just One Straight Nerf
content:
Seventeen guns changed for Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone Season 1. Only the Apoc-338 took a straight nerf, while rifles and SMGs gained…

Seventeen weapons have balance changes for Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone Season 1, and the Apoc-338 is the only straight nerf, Dexerto reported. Fourteen guns received buffs only.

The Hyeon Burst and VEL 46 got a mix of both.

Season 1 arrives November 6. The official Call of Duty blog lists further weapon balance adjustments among the changes alongside the full integration of Warzone with Modern Warfare 4.

That integration, covered in our Season 1 overview , includes a Player Level reset and access to all 33 launch weapons.

The Axion has its first medium damage range stretched from 34.8 m to 38.61 m, and its muzzle velocity rises from 415 m/s to 470 m/s. The Kastov 762 gains a point of damage in its first medium tier (24 to 25), with its range there growing from 40.13 m to 42.16 m. Its head multiplier moves from 1.33 to 1.35.

title: Road Rash Returns on PC as EA Re-Releases 25 Classic Games on Steam and GOG
content:
Road Rash is back. EA has re-released the 1996 PC version of its motorcycle combat racer as Road Rash: 30th Anniversary Edition, one of 25 classic games that launched on Steam, GOG and the EA app on November 5, 2026. The Anniversary Editions cost $9.99 each, and the other 18 games cost $4.99, with launch discounts running until November 19.

This is not a new Road Rash or a reboot. It is the original game, restored, with modern touches such as controller support and cloud saves. For anyone who grew up kicking rival bikers off the road, that is probably the better news.

The Anniversary Edition is the 1996 PC release of Road Rash, not the original 1991 Mega Drive version. That PC version is the one many players remember for its full-motion video cutscenes and its licensed soundtrack, which included Soundgarden, Monster Magnet and Therapy?. EA says the soundtrack is included.

On top of that, EA has added a short list of modern improvements, according to Beebom:

Road Rash is the headline name, but most of the collection comes from Origin Systems, the studio behind Wing Commander and Ultima. Seven games get the fuller Anniversary Edition treatment.

The other 18 games cost $4.99 each. They include Wing Commander: Privateer, Academy and Armada, Strike Commander, Theme Hospital, Crusader: No Remorse and No Regret, all nine Ultima games and both Ultima Underworld games.

title: Counter-Strike Hall of Fame 2026: Rambo Is One of Three Americans on the Ballot
content:
Ronald "Rambo" Kim is a first-time nominee for the Counter-Strike Hall of Fame, alongside fRoD and Ksharp. Four of 10 will be inducted in…

Ronald "Rambo" Kim, a 42-year-old veteran of Counter-Strike's earliest LAN events, is a first-time nominee for the HLTV Hall of Fame, dust2.us reported.

He is one of three Americans among the 10 players up for the Class of 2026.

HLTV says the class will be inducted at the HLTV Awards in Belgrade, Serbia, on January 9, 2027. Pley (pley.gg) reports that only four of the 10 nominees will make it in.

The ballot reaches back to the original game, well before Counter-Strike 2 .

Kim competed at Babbage's CPL 2000, one of the game's first major LAN events.

title: VCT 2027 : Riot verrouille la triche avant les qualifications ouvertes
content:
À l’approche des qualifications ouvertes du VCT 2027, Riot Games a détaillé dans un article les mesures qui encadreront l’accès à la scène compétitive de VALORANT. Tous les compétiteurs devront être conformes aux vérifications Vanguard, et les joueurs devront atteindre au minimum le rang Ascendant pour participer à ces qualifications.

La saison 2027 s’ouvre à plus d’équipes, avec davantage de voies de qualification et le retour des compétitions en ligne. Riot veut sécuriser ces nouvelles portes d’entrée. Les joueurs dont les comptes sont en règle restent éligibles, mais certains comptes pourront faire l’objet d’examens supplémentaires, précise l’éditeur.

Riot Games pose deux conditions cumulatives. D’une part, les vérifications Vanguard, l’anti-cheat de VALORANT, s’appliqueront à tous les compétiteurs. D’autre part, le rang Ascendant devient le plancher requis pour les qualifications ouvertes. Pour les joueurs qui visent ces qualifications, ces deux exigences sont donc un préalable, et non une option.

L’éditeur ne précise pas encore la date d’ouverture de ces qualifications, seulement annoncées comme à venir. Les joueurs concernés ont donc intérêt à surveiller leur compte et leur rang.

Riot Games applique une politique de tolérance zéro concernant la triche. L’éditeur rappelle aussi que faciliter ou aider autrui à tricher est interdit, ce qui élargit le cadre au-delà du seul joueur qui triche. Cette position s’accompagne de mesures techniques : exigences de sécurité matérielles et logicielles plus strictes, critères d’éligibilité clairs pour les comptes et surveillance supplémentaire.

L’objectif affiché par Riot est triple : prévenir la triche avant qu’elle ne survienne, détecter les activités suspectes et garantir des conditions équitables à chaque équipe. Dans cet article, l’éditeur ne cite ni équipe ni joueur, et n’annonce aucune sanction nominative. La communication reste donc préventive.

title: ‘Is This Who We Are Now?’ Leicester Fans Turn on Shirt Sponsor BC.Game Over Eva Elfie Deal
content:
Leicester City’s supporters’ trust has turned on the club’s front-of-shirt sponsor BC.Game, after the crypto casino signed Russian adult film star Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador. In a statement headlined “It gets worse” and published on 4 November, the Foxes Trust said the deal links gambling and pornography to Leicester City by association. Its blunt question to supporters, “Is this who we are now?”, has since been viewed more than 150,000 times on X. Within a day, the club had confirmed that it had raised the concerns directly with BC.Game, which has sponsored the Leicester shirt since 2024.

BC.Game, which also owns s1mple’s Counter-Strike 2 team, announced Elfie as its newest ambassador on 3 November, presenting her as an “international content creator and esports personality”. According to the company, the partnership covers content collaborations, promotional campaigns and appearances at sports and esports events. Chief executive Ali “Ako” Muhanned said she “has built an incredible relationship with the gaming and esports community”. The Foxes Trust was far less polite, describing her as someone “who continues to make their name via adult content”.

The Trust has opposed BC.Game’s sponsorship since it was first announced in July 2024, when it said that a gambling website on the shirt was another step away from Leicester’s “well run family club” reputation. Its latest statement goes further, arguing that the club picked a gambling company that is “unlicensed to operate in the UK” and lets customers play with cryptocurrencies. It also says BC.Game “has unanswered questions about the legitimacy of its funding and its origins”.

The objection is not only about BC.Game’s business model, however. “Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people’s lives, in particular young people,” the statement reads, adding that partnerships like this bring both worlds to a larger audience. The Trust also points to its end-of-season survey, in which 73% of fans said they felt negative about the BC.Game relationship and only 5% were content with it. Its advice to supporters has not changed since 2024 either: anyone buying a replica shirt should pick one without the BC.Game logo on it.

Leicester’s own response, by contrast, has been noticeably more cautious. A club spokesperson told the BBC that Leicester “recognises the concerns raised about recent developments” and had taken them up directly with the sponsor. The club added that it is “continuing discussions with the company to explore a mutually acceptable resolution”, wording that stops well short of saying the deal is under threat. When Leicester first announced the partnership in 2024, it described BC.Game as a “socially responsible platform”, and the BBC notes that the company’s services are not available to users in the UK.

BC.Game became Leicester’s principal partner in July 2024, a few months after the club had won promotion back to the Premier League, in a deal the company’s own press release valued at $40 million. Trouble followed within months, when the Norwegian football outlet Josimar reported that Curaçao’s gaming regulator was moving to revoke the licence held by the company behind BC.Game. There were also reports of a bankruptcy case brought by customers in Curaçao, although BC.Game strongly denied the accusations and assured the club that it was appealing and had no liquidity issues.

title: Worlds 2026 : Bilibili Gaming écrase Dplus KIA et poursuit son massacre de la LCK
content:
Bilibili Gaming est décidément le bourreau de la LCK dans ces championnats du monde. Déjà tombeurs de Hanwha Life Esports lors de l’ultime round du Swiss Stage, les Chinois ont récidivé cette nuit face à Dplus KIA, sans laisser la moindre chance à ShowMaker et ses coéquipiers. Dès la première manche, BLG a surpris son adversaire avec un choix audacieux à la draft : une Cassiopeia pour Viper sur la botlane. Un pari rapidement récompensé sur la Faille de l’invocateur, où les représentants de la LPL ont imposé leur rythme. Impérial sur Nautilus, ON a multiplié les initiatives décisives, tandis que XUN a littéralement massacré les rangs coréens avec sa Naafiri, terminant la partie sur un impressionnant 12/1/8.

MAIS ON EST TOTALEMENT FOU ?! pic.twitter.com/p3BCkpFVs4

La deuxième manche n’a fait que confirmer l’écart entre les deux formations. Cette fois, c’est Viper qui s’est particulièrement illustré avec son Ezreal (5/2/7), multipliant les dégâts dans les affrontements. Déjà irréprochable sur Galio lors de la première partie, Knight a poursuivi sa démonstration avec une Orianna parfaitement maîtrisée (2/0/8). Supérieurs dans les teamfights comme dans la gestion de la carte, les Chinois ont une nouvelle fois étouffé leurs adversaires, incapables de trouver la moindre ouverture. À 2-0, Dplus KIA semblait déjà condamné face à une équipe de BLG particulièrement impressionnante.

Dos au mur, les Coréens n’ont pas réussi à inverser la tendance dans la troisième manche. Malgré les efforts de ShowMaker et de ses jeunes coéquipiers, Dplus KIA s’est encore heurté à l’expérience et à la maîtrise collective des Chinois. Cette fois, Bin s’est chargé de porter le coup de grâce avec son Jax signature, concluant la rencontre sur des statistiques monstrueuses : 12 éliminations, 4 morts et 5 assists. La domination de BLG s’est également traduite dans le contrôle des objectifs neutres, avec un bilan hallucinant de 14 dragons récupérés contre un seul pour DK sur l’ensemble du BO5. Une statistique qui résume parfaitement le fossé entre les deux équipes.

Les coachs célèbrent déjà à 4 min mdrrr pic.twitter.com/3XCJAVEl5R

Comme Gen.G face à LYON la veille, Bilibili Gaming valide donc son billet pour les demi-finales sur un 3-0 sans appel. Pour Dplus KIA, l’aventure mondiale s’arrête brutalement en quart de finale, malgré une saison 2026 marquée notamment par son sacre à l’Esports World Cup. De son côté, BLG confirme son statut de sérieux prétendant au titre et attend désormais le vainqueur du choc entre T1 et la Karmine Corp. Une chose est certaine : après Hanwha Life et Dplus, les Chinois n’ont visiblement pas peur des géants coréens.

title: G2’s 2027 Rebuild: No Head Coach, SkewMond Stuck on a Buyout and Two Starters Days From Free Agency
content:
G2 Esports have gone from Europe’s most settled super team to the busiest project of the LEC off-season in barely a week. The club that swept every domestic title in 2026 now has no head coach, a star jungler it will not release for free and two starters whose contracts run out on 16 November. On top of that, G2 have told fans they will not confirm any changes until free agency officially opens.

The upheaval began with the reports that Lyncas is set to replace SkewMond in the jungle after G2’s early Worlds 2026 exit. It accelerated on 5 November, when G2 ended their collaboration with head coach Perkz hours after his long personal statement on X. Here is where every piece of the G2 Esports roster now stands.

The core of the team is still tied down for now. Caps, the club’s longest-serving player, is under contract until November 2027, while Hans Sama and SkewMond both have deals running until November 2028. The bigger short-term risk sits at the two ends of the map. Top laner BrokenBlade and support Labrov both become free agents on 16 November, and no new agreement had been reached with either of them, according to Sheep Esports.

That makes the next 10 days critical for G2’s management. If both players leave, G2 could be replacing three of the five starters who completed this year’s Golden Road, a sweep of the LEC Versus, Spring and Summer titles. They would also be doing it without the head coach who led them to the record 20th LEC title in September . For a team that has stayed broadly stable since 2024, it would be the biggest reset since G2 moved on from Yike and Mikyx two years ago.

SkewMond’s situation is the most awkward of all. The Frenchman extended his contract until November 2028 in February, and he went on to be named Spring Finals MVP and, by many accounts, the team’s best player of the year. Even so, G2 have decided to move on from him, and the club is reportedly not prepared to release him for free, demanding a buyout fee from any team that wants him instead.

Several LEC teams could be in the market for a new jungler. Fnatic , Karmine Corp , Team Vitality, Shifters, GIANTX and SK Gaming all face decisions in that role, although G2 may be reluctant to sell their former starter to a direct LEC rival. That would leave a move to North America as one possible outcome, which would cost Europe one of its brightest young players.

title: Discord Is Ditching Electron, And Its New Rust Client Runs Two Accounts in Just 290 MB of RAM
content:
Discord is finally getting rid of Electron, the web-based framework behind its desktop app for years. Co-founder and chief technology officer Stanislav Vishnevskiy has confirmed that the company is rebuilding its entire client in Rust . An early Windows build, codenamed Discord Phoenix, is already running at a fraction of the memory the current app uses. In a screenshot he shared on 4 November, Windows Task Manager showed Discord Phoenix at just 290.2 MB while it was signed in to two accounts at once.

For a desktop app that players have complained about for years, that is a dramatic change. Vishnevskiy wrote that Discord has been an early adopter of Rust since 2018, and that much of its infrastructure, voice technology and even parts of the current client already use it. “The holy grail was getting the whole client there,” he added. He confirmed that the new desktop interface is built with GPUI , the GPU-accelerated UI framework made by the team behind the Zed code editor, rather than with Tauri , as many people had guessed.

We've been early adopters of Rust since 2018 and a lot of our infra, voice tech, and even some of the current client is already Rust, the holy grail was getting the whole client there. That means Electron goes away, and so does React Native, mobile keeps native UI but shares app… https://t.co/2CgWyOzaq0 pic.twitter.com/IdOGd4nUgl

The screenshot is more revealing than the headline number. Discord Phoenix appears as a single entry with no child processes, while the apps around it are split into several. Google Chrome sits at 1,568.6 MB across 19 processes, the Steam Client WebHelper at 856 MB across seven and Notion at 932.5 MB across nine, so the contrast with a native app is plain to see.

Vishnevskiy also used the replies to explain what users can expect. He said the new client “looks and works identically to the current one”. It also has full multi-account support on desktop and mobile, so you can even sit in voice channels on two accounts at the same time. When one user joked about the RAM figure, he pointed out that the build in the screenshot was running two accounts concurrently, a feature the new client supports.

Vishnevskiy has also made it clear that the change goes well beyond memory. A day after the screenshot, he posted a boot-time comparison filmed on two older laptops. “Clicking around feels instant, I can’t go back,” he wrote, in a post that has since passed 1.8 million views among PC players who keep Discord running next to their games.

title: Nvidia Sheds $450 Billion in a day as AI Chip Rout Wipes $2.3 Trillion From the Nasdaq-100
content:
Nvidia had one of the worst days in its recent history on Thursday, as a brutal selloff in AI and chip stocks wiped out gains that had taken months to build. The world’s most valuable chipmaker closed at $181.60 on the Nasdaq , down $18.53 or 9.26%, which erased roughly $450 billion of market value in a single session. That left Nvidia worth about $4.4 trillion, and its shares are now down nearly a quarter from their record close on 6 October.

Measured from that peak, roughly $1.4 trillion has disappeared from Nvidia’s valuation in a month. The damage was not limited to one company, though, because Nvidia is also a member of the Dow Jones Industrial Average , which plunged 1,833.06 points. Across the wider tech sector, the Nasdaq-100 lost about $2.3 trillion in value during the day, according to Yahoo Finance’s market coverage.

Every major US index closed sharply lower, and all three of the best-known benchmarks recorded their worst day since April 2025. The Dow finished at 51,523.06, down 3.44%, while the S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.52% to 24,315, a fall that pushed it into correction territory, more than 10% below its own record close on 6 October.

The real carnage, however, was concentrated in semiconductor stocks. The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 12.25% to 9,011.14, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF had its worst day since March 2020, according to CNBC. Wall Street’s fear gauge, the VIX, also jumped to around 28 during the session, its highest level since 31 March.

Several of Nvidia’s peers fared even worse in percentage terms. Micron fell 17.46% to $656.39 and AMD dropped 17.26% to $404.40, while Arm lost 13.08%, Broadcom 10.43% and Intel 10.33%. For Intel, it extends a slide that had already cut its value almost in half in the space of a few weeks.

Qualcomm added a company-specific problem to the mix. Its quarterly results showed phone chip sales down 26%, missing Wall Street estimates on weak demand and lower Apple-related revenue, and the stock closed 9.49% lower. AMD chief executive Lisa Su struck a philosophical tone as her company’s shares tumbled, telling Yahoo Finance that “the market can sometimes be a little bit short-sighted.”

title: Pilot Spends Eight Hours Drawing GTA 6 in the Sky Over Arkansas
content:
An American pilot has drawn GTA 6 in the sky. Benjamin G. McDaniel III, known online as “The Pilot Picasso”, flew a 1978 Cessna 182 Skylane RG over Arkansas for more than eight hours, tracing the Grand Theft Auto VI logo and artwork from the game’s official cover with his flight path. The flight ran from November 5 into November 6 and could be followed live on Flightradar24.

With GTA 6 less than two weeks from launch, it is one of the more unusual fan tributes so far. You cannot see the drawing from the ground. It only appears on the flight-tracking map, where the plane’s route turns into a picture.

McDaniel took off from Bentonville Municipal Airport in north-west Arkansas, according to Beebom. Over the course of the flight, his track recreated the GTA 6 logo along with details from the cover art: a woman holding a pistol, a sports car, an alligator, palm trees and a helicopter at the top.

Every line in a drawing like this has to be planned in advance and flown precisely. One wrong turn shows up on the map for good. McDaniel has described the work as a single attempt, telling Rotate Pilot in an earlier interview that “you get one shot”.

GTA 6 is not McDaniel’s first big subject. He has previously traced the Mona Lisa over Oklahoma, Edvard Munch’s The Scream over Missouri, and Spider-Man, which made him a familiar name in GPS art circles.

A video game is a fun change of pace from classical paintings, and there are few games with more pull right now than GTA 6.

title: Xbox PC App Now Launches Up to 60% Faster in New Insider Update
content:
Microsoft has started testing a rebuilt Xbox app for PC that launches up to 60% faster than the current version. The new app is available now to members of the Xbox Insider programme, and Microsoft says Store and Game Pass pages also load up to 50% faster.

Speed has been the most common complaint about the Xbox app on Windows, especially for players with large libraries. This update goes straight at that problem, and also tidies up how you find games, friends and add-ons.

These are Microsoft’s own figures, as reported by iXBT.games, and they are “up to” numbers, so real-world gains will depend on your PC and your library size.

Early hands-on testing backs up the direction, if not the exact numbers. Windows Central’s Jez Corden tried an early build of the new app, codenamed Garrison, with a library of more than 1,400 Xbox games and found it “a lot faster than the previous app” at loading it. That is exactly the kind of library that used to make the old app crawl.

The rebuilt app also changes how you get around. The Library has new filters for sorting your games. The friends list now sits in the main menu, so you can message someone without digging through extra screens. Search has been unified, so one search box now finds games, add-ons and other players in one place.

Light, dark and high-contrast themes are also on the way. The high-contrast option is a welcome accessibility addition for players who find the current dark interface hard to read.

title: Take-Two CEO Admits GTA 6 Will Be Pirated, Says Company Is Ready
content:
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick has accepted that GTA 6 will be pirated, and says the company is ready for it. Speaking in an interview with WSJ Tech, Zelnick called piracy an unavoidable part of the entertainment business that companies have to plan around, not wish away, according to a report by iXBT.games.

It is a frank admission two weeks before launch. GTA 6 releases on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and Take-Two says it is prepared to add more technical protection and take legal action if piracy reaches a serious scale.

To make his point, Zelnick looked at other industries, as reported by iXBT.games. In film, pirated copies have at times made up 10% to 20% of the market. In music, the share reportedly hit around 80% in the mid-2000s before streaming pulled it back down.

Games, he argued, are in a stronger position than either. The figures above are as Zelnick described them in the interview, not independent data.

Zelnick pointed to three things that make modern games harder to pirate. The first is size. GTA 6 is reported to need around 210GB on PS5, which makes it a slow and awkward file to pass around. The second is the hardware itself. Current consoles are much harder to modify than older machines. The third is updates. Regular patches from the developer can break pirated copies, and online features usually need a legitimate account.

That last point matters most for GTA. Much of the long-term value of GTA 5 came from GTA Online, and an online mode is very hard to use with a pirated copy. Our breakdown of how much space GTA 6 takes on each PS5 model shows just how big the install is.

title: Apex Legends Godzilla Event: Every Skin, Event Pass Rewards and Dates
content:
Godzilla is coming to Apex Legends. The Godzilla event runs from November 10 to December 1, 2026, and brings ten kaiju-themed legend skins, nine legendary weapon skins, a new universal melee weapon and an Event Pass with free and premium rewards, according to EA’s official event page .

The event takes place on Storm Point, and EA’s pitch is simple: “You can’t defeat it, you can only survive.” The headline cosmetics are Iconic skins that turn legends into Godzilla, Mothra, Mechagodzilla and other famous monsters from the films.

Nine of the ten legend skins are Iconic, the top rarity for collaboration cosmetics. Each one is named after a specific version of a monster, so long-time Godzilla fans will spot the film years.

Pathfinder as Mechagodzilla and Revenant as Super Mechagodzilla are natural fits for the two robot legends. Bloodhound gets the newest version of the big guy himself. EA has not listed prices for the skins outside the Event Pass yet.

The Event Pass has two tracks. Everyone gets the free one, and the premium track costs 950 Apex Coins.

title: KRAFTON India’s KIGI PitchFest: 8 Indie Studios Picked From 300+ Entries
content:
KRAFTON India’s push to build a home-grown game development scene took centre stage in Chennai last week, as eight indie studios pitched their games at the fourth edition of KIGI PitchFest. The studios were shortlisted from more than 300 applications, all of which came in within 30 days of entries opening. They presented on 30 October at the Chennai Trade Centre, during the India Game Developer Conference (IGDC) 2026 , in front of a crowd of more than 100 people.

The format itself left very little room for padding or long introductions. Each studio had 10 minutes to pitch its game and show gameplay, before facing another 10 minutes of questions from the jury. According to KRAFTON India, the teams that made the shortlist stood out for having a playable build and a clear pitch deck. It also looked for strong alignment between the founders, their teams and the goals of the KRAFTON India Gaming Incubator (KIGI) . That emphasis on playable builds is telling, because it rewards teams that have already put months of work into a game rather than those with only an idea.

The shortlisted studios were AbhiTechGames, Arckon Arts, Team Quasar, Compiling Shaders Games, Kalp, Xigma Games, Tandoori Pixels and 2Tellers Studio. KRAFTON India has not yet shared the games, genres or home cities of the eight teams, although it said the lineup covered a wide range of genres and platforms. They pitched to a 12-member jury drawn from India, South Korea and the United States, with expertise spanning product, design, art and strategy.

Anuj Sahani, who heads the KRAFTON India Incubator Programme, said the company was “encouraged by the overwhelming response to KIGI PitchFest this year”. He added that “it is great to see India’s indie gaming community building momentum”, and thanked the jury for the perspectives it brought to the sessions. Beyond the jury’s verdict, the studios also had the chance to collect feedback, meet mentors and connect with industry figures across the conference.

The stakes are significant for small teams working on tight budgets. Studios selected for KIGI receive between $50,000 and $150,000 in financial support, along with hands-on mentoring from industry veterans and access to KRAFTON’s resources. The programme can also open doors to publishing support, venture capital and potential equity investment from KRAFTON itself.

KRAFTON India launched the incubator in 2023, and its first two cohorts brought in 10 studios between them. The third cohort followed in April 2026, when KIGI added four more studios , Xod Games Studio, EvolX Games, Ether Games and RedDevil Studio, from roughly 1,000 applications. In September, KRAFTON opened Cohort 4 with wider eligibility, inviting mobile games already in beta or soft launch and PC games with a live Steam demo, alongside early-stage teams with only a concept.

title: How to Play GTA 6 Early on Xbox and PS5 Using the New Zealand Trick
content:
GTA 6 will not unlock everywhere at once. Rockstar Games has confirmed a rolling release, with the game going live at midnight local time on November 19 in each region. New Zealand is first, at 11:00 UTC on November 18, which is 18 hours before players on the US East Coast get in.

That gap has led to a familiar trick: switch your console or account to New Zealand and start playing hours early. It can work on both Xbox and PS5, but it is not the same process on each, and the PlayStation version comes with real downsides.

Here is when the New Zealand unlock lands in other time zones, and how many hours earlier that is than each region’s own midnight release, based on the regional schedule reported by GamingBible.

The further west you are, the more you gain. For players in Australia, the trick is barely worth the effort. For anyone in the Americas, it turns launch night into launch morning.

On Xbox Series X|S, the region is tied to the console’s location setting, so no VPN or new account is needed. Go to Profile & System, then Settings, System and Language & Location. Set the location to New Zealand and restart the console.

Once the game unlocks in New Zealand, it should start for you too, as long as you have already bought it and finished the pre-load. You can switch back afterwards. Bear in mind that changing region can also change what the Microsoft Store shows you until you switch it back.

title: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 Weapon Buffs and Nerfs: Every Gun That Changed
content:
Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 brings 18 weapon balance changes to multiplayer, and almost all of them are buffs. Only the APOC-338 LMG takes a straight nerf, while the HYEON BURST and VEL 46 get a mix of ups and downs. The rest gain damage, range or both.

The pattern is clear once you read the numbers. Infinity Ward is pulling weaker guns up rather than knocking the strongest ones down, so expect your loadout options to widen rather than shrink this season.

Six assault rifles change in Season 1, more than any other class. Most of the gains are in range and headshot damage, which rewards players who can hold their aim at mid distance.

The AXION change is the one to try first. A jump from 415 to 470 m/s muzzle velocity means bullets reach long-range targets noticeably faster, and it comes with almost four extra metres of medium-damage range.

The WZ.55 STRIGA comes out of this as the big winner among SMGs. A head multiplier of 1.4 is the highest on this list, and the two-point bump to minimum damage helps it in fights it used to lose at range. The VEL 46 goes the other way. Its damage drops off sooner, though a higher damage floor softens the blow.

The APOC-338 has been one of the most popular LMGs since launch, so a small trim was expected. It is still a strong option. The TYPE 73 is now a more serious alternative, especially with its Apex attachment.

title: SAG-AFTRA Deal Lets Developers Hire Union Actors for Game Pitch Demos
content:
SAG-AFTRA has launched a new contract that lets game developers hire union actors before their game has any funding. The Pre-Funding Pitch Interactive Media Agreement covers early material made to win over publishers and investors, from an internal teaser trailer to a playable vertical slice.

In practice, that means a small studio pitching its first game could put a professional voice actor or motion-capture performer in its demo, on union terms, before a single publisher has signed on. The one major exception is crowdfunding. Games funded through platforms such as Kickstarter are not covered.

The agreement is built for the earliest stage of development, when a studio has an idea and a prototype but no money to finish the game. Developers can bring in union talent to perform in pitch material that shows backers what the finished game could look like.

SAG-AFTRA has not published rates or the full terms alongside the announcement, as reported by VGC. It is also unclear exactly what counts as a pitch demo and what happens to a performance if the game later gets funded. Those details will matter most to the studios and actors who use it.

SAG-AFTRA president Sean Astin, best known for playing Sam in The Lord of the Rings, said the deal is about “bringing in professional voice and motion performance talent earlier in the process.”

Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, the union’s national executive director and chief negotiator, said the agreement “streamlines the hiring of professional union talent.” In other words, a developer who wants a union actor in a pitch no longer has to work out which full contract applies to a project that may never exist.

title: Alfajer leaves FNATIC, ending a four-year run

In a score of three games to one, Natus Vincere reigned supreme over GamerLegion as they quickly shut down the hopes of the top North American Dota 2 team of getting a trophy at EPL Masters III, a Tier 3 tournament.

One of Natus Vincere’s biggest strengths is their players’ deep hero pools. Throughout their upper-bracket run, they rarely picked the same heroes twice, instead focusing on countering their opponents through smart drafting. Some of their most successful picks in the tournament include Brewmaster, Kez, and Dazzle.

During the grand final against GamerLegion, NAVI’s offlaner Yurii “pma” Prots stole the show with his Brewmaster and Timbersaw, playing a key role in their wins across Games 1, 2, and 3. He also kept his net worth close to that of his other cores while recording no more than four deaths, an impressive feat for an offlane role that often requires taking risky initiations and absorbing pressure.

title: Overwatch Terms of Justice recap: New Helix hero plus Soldier: 76, Reaper, Cassidy, and Sojourn reunion
content:
Overwatch’s newest story, “Terms of Justice” arrived shortly after the “All That Follows” featuring Doomfist’s Talon , giving players a look into what’s happening on Sojourn’s side of the narrative. Here is esports.gg’s recap of the new Overwatch story plus some of our theories of what’s next for the narrative.

“Terms of Justice” begins with Sojourn recalling her testimony to the International Justice Commission (IJC) against Overwatch all those years ago. She acknowledges that although her emotions got the better of her back then, she spoke nothing but the truth.

Sojourn then remembers how Jack Morrison, also now known as Soldier: 76, used to value saving lives more than following the rules. One day, however, Jack Morrison’s choices caught up to him and the IJC shut Overwatch down .

Now, Sojourn is facing those same difficult decisions. She recalls how Cassidy stood by the reunited Overwatch crew and held off the Deadlock Gang at Watchpoint: Grand Mesa . Meanwhile, Genji went to Japan to stop Vendetta’s Talon from gaining access to a lot of anima weapons and D.Va’s connection to the MEKA Squad saved thousands of lives. She also remembers saving people during the recent battle in Rome against Vendetta’s forces .

Before Sojourn’s meeting with IJC representative Osei, she fondly thinks about Tracer and Winston fighting by her side. She’s concerned about the fate of Echo, Juno, and Mizuki as well.

When Sojourn finally talks to Osei, the latter tells her that her Overwatch agents don’t need to leave at all. Instead, Osei wants to renew Overwatch’s charter to make the organization a legal one again. Sojourn wonders what the catch is, and Osei reveals that “a Helix general” will monitor all of Overwatch’s missions moving forward.
